text:
anya: heads up — after the quantized rollout we saw a 12-20% p99 regression on short chat requests. suspect kernel switching + cold KV-cache warmup. can someone sanity-check an nsys capture recipe?

zack: oof. can you reproduce locally with single-GPU and a small batch that hits the short path? if so, use bracketed capture around the inference span. NVTX bracketing is easiest.

anya: repro is stable on my dev box. example flow: load model -> run 5 warmup inferences -> run 50 test inferences (short ~64 tokens).

maria: for short bursts i prefer a tiny bracketed capture to avoid noisy kernel sampling. pattern i use: NVTX push before the 50 tests, pop after. then nsys profile with osrt sampling and cuda trace.

zack: concrete flags i used recently (works well for capture size and kernel timeline clarity):
```
nsys profile \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=nvtx:mybracket:start:mybracket:end \
  --sample=cpu --cpuctx-switches=true \
  --output=out_qdrep \
  --duration=8s
```
NOTE: replace --sample=cpu with --sample=none if you only want event traces. duration should be just slightly longer than your bracket window.

anya: thanks — what about sample-window / short duration bias? i remember short captures can miss infrequent kernels (prefetch, eviction).

maria: yup. two heuristics: 1) include a tiny pre-bracket steady-state (1–2s) so the sampler warms, 2) if you care about KV-eviction events, extend capture to include the earlier warmup + a few post-calls. but that increases file size.

zack: also add NVTX markers around quantization/loader and around the KV access code so you can filter timeline by those labels in UI. e.g. 
```
NVTX_MARKER("kv_lookup_start");
// lookup
NVTX_MARKER("kv_lookup_end");
```
Then filter on nvtx tags to see kernel ordering vs kv hits.

anya: perf-bot ran a quick baseline capture and attached a snippet of kernel timeline (copied here):
perf-bot: [auto-capture] timeline: long memset, then small kernel bursts, then a big convolution switch at 120ms, followed by a short memcpy stall at 190ms.

maria: that pattern screams a kernel selection fallback mid-sequence. likely sequence-length dependent kernel choice. check allocator stats for cuBLAS/cuDNN fallback too.

zack: run a comparison capture with and without prefix caching to isolate if KV cache warmup causes different batching patterns. i usually run two captures back-to-back: one with prefix cached (mock keys) and one cold.

anya: note: when i forced the kv cache to hit, p99 dropped back down ~8%. so kv warmup is definitely contributing. need to validate whether it triggers different kernel launch params or just causes extra memcpy.

maria: quick debug commands:
```
# bracketed run with NVTX markers (short)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx:run:start:run:end --output=run1 --duration=6s
# non-bracketed longer run (for sampling rare kernels)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run_long --duration=30s
```
open both .qdrep files in Nsight and compare kernel rows and timeline heatmap. look at OSRT metrics to see which op consumed most host CPU time.

anya: any guidance on sampling frequency toggles? i see --sample options but docs are fuzzy.

zack: nsys sampling mostly toggles CPU sampling. for GPU kernels rely on event traces + NVTX. if you suspect missed short kernels, increase capture duration, or run repeated short-bracket captures offset by 1s to probabilistically sample. annoying but effective.

maria: also check the 'CUDA API' lane for cuBLAS/cuDNN workspace alloc/free patterns. frequent small allocs can create fragmentation and memcpy stalls.

anya: great checklist. i'll run: 1) bracketed short capture with nvtx markers, 2) long capture for rare kernel sampling, 3) compare cached vs cold KV, 4) check cuBLAS allocs. will post the two qdrep exports here.

zack: ping us when uploads are up. if kernel switch is confirmed, we can add a quick runtime change to prefer the short-sequence kernel for the quantized variant while we dig deeper. :thumbsup:

maria: also file a perf regression PR with the two captures attached and a small repro script so CI can catch regressions.

anya: thanks all — running now, will upload qdrep in ~10m.
